name: Site progress photography — capture as contemporaneous record
one_line: The organizational situation in which a deliberately repeated or issued photographic record evidences the state of construction work over time: site-walk sets, pre-cover-up sequences, annotated captures and generated photo reports. It is not the image SOURCE_TYPE, a photo format, a date, a site or a work stage; those are evidence channels or values. It stands only when purpose-bearing record structure or an accepted construction-project or site-diary relationship distinguishes the captures from an ordinary camera event. Absorbs the legacy row cons.progress-photos (ROW). Placeholder: it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a deliberately repeated capture series at an already-supported construction site, with comparable viewpoints across accepted site walks or diary dates and evidence of changing works. Repetition of place across time is corroboration only: the same pattern also describes a home-security camera, a garden diary or routine property inspection. “EXIF is strong photo evidence; capture time, GPS, and sensor-shaped dimensions reinforce it; exact display resolutions, PNG format, and software metadata may support a screenshot hypothesis; conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification.”

camera EXIF present and consistent, but only as proof of capture provenance inside a purpose-bearing progress set: a device make and model, DateTimeOriginal, and sensor-shaped dimensions do not themselves identify construction or progress. “HEIC support must be included explicitly, because failing to configure the image stack for HEIC can silently exclude a meaningful portion of an Apple-centric corpus.”

an annotated or stamped capture: a date-and-time overlay burned into the frame, a site name watermark, or a compass and coordinate stamp from a site-photo application - a deliberate self-evidencing mark that ordinary photography does not carry.

a photo-report document: a generated PDF or presentation of dated, captioned images in a grid, with a site header and a reference - the form the photographs are usually delivered in and the form that survives.

an image whose subject matter shows changing construction work - excavations, reinforcement before a pour, service runs before they are boarded, scaffolding - when that content occurs in a repeated, captioned, issued or accepted project/diary set. Structural subject matter alone is never activation.

an accepted construction-project or site-diary group that gives otherwise sparse captures their record purpose. The relationship supports membership; it does not copy a site, date, stage or any other missing fact onto the image. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

the same device, the same day, two purposes: a site manager's phone holds the progress walk and a photograph of their lunch, and only content decides. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”

separating a progress record from a defect record, a delivery record, an inventory record and a damage claim - all site photography, all from the same phone, distinguished only by what the image shows and what group it joins.
reading a caption or an embedded annotation as the thing that gives an image its meaning, when the filename is IMG_ and nothing else.
deciding whether a set of images without EXIF - stripped by a messaging app on the way from a subcontractor - is a progress set at all.
recognising a photo-report PDF as a derived document of an image set that also exists loose in the corpus.
never_alone: the absence of EXIF read as proof of anything. 00 is explicit that the system “must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot.” and the mirror error matters more here: site photographs routinely ARRIVE stripped, forwarded through messaging apps, and their being stripped says nothing about what they are.

an image file alone. This is the row's constitutional never-alone: an image is a source_type, and “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”
a GPS coordinate alone. It locates a capture; it does not say the capture was a record rather than a snapshot, and a domestic job's coordinates are somebody's home.
a capture date alone - every image has one.
a work stage alone - excavation, pre-pour, first fix and completion are values describing what work is shown, and the same words occur in programmes, diaries, defect lists and ordinary captions.
a device make and model alone: the same phone takes the progress walk, the family photographs and the screenshots.

a site or client name in a folder name alone, read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”

membership in a download session that pulled a month of site images at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

work_types: photograph of a document taken on site (boundary case, not this row)
grouping_reasons: one site walk: images sharing a device, a date and a place, which is the natural unit and the one a person recognises. Time is genuinely the organizing axis here, unlike everywhere else on this schema.
one element across time: the same corner of a building photographed every week, which is the comparison the pictures exist to support and which no single capture date expresses.
one photo report and the loose images it was generated from, which is a derived-document relationship rather than a duplicate one.

a capture set and the site diary entry or valuation it substantiates - purpose-coherent and content-incoherent, and a real reason to join files without copying any fact between them. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
no group at all is a valid outcome, and common: a single photograph sent to answer a question is an image with no event association.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: construction_property declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields, and this row's recommendation is genuinely unlike its siblings': SITE or job first, then the capture date, and nothing below that. Time is the leaf that carries the meaning, because the whole value of the archive is that a given date can be produced on demand. The flag is nonetheless recorded as time_first = false, and deliberately so: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - a year-first tree would scatter one site's record across calendar folders and destroy the week-to-week comparison the photographs exist for. A site is a project, and the project comes first. That is the honest reading of the rule for this row even though the row is capture-based; the photos schema's own camera-events template is the situation where time genuinely leads, and this row is deliberately not that. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” - a capture date means nothing without knowing which site it was taken at. Privacy caveat specific to this row: site photographs contain workers' faces, vehicle registrations, neighbouring private property, and GPS to the metre - for domestic work, a private person's home - and none of that should acquire automatic depth or reach a model prompt by default. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem.

collides_with.signal: The project row is the branch root that gives these captures their job context but does not own their photographic evidence. A contract envelope, programme, award sequence or handover pack supports the project row; a deliberately repeated, annotated or issued photographic record supports this row. The same IMG_2044.HEIC may join an accepted project without the project copying site, date or stage facts onto it. Conversely, a project folder containing loose images does not activate this row unless the photographic-record situation is independently supported.

The row's defining collision uses the same bytes: the same phone capture and the same EXIF can support the photos schema while a construction relationship supports this situation. Camera EXIF, capture time and GPS support camera-events; they never prove progress. A deliberately repeated, captioned, issued or project/diary-associated record of changing works supports this row. A camera make, capture date, GPS point, weekday rhythm, site name or structural subject alone discriminates neither, and both schema readings may remain true of one file.

A defect close-up and a progress frame are adjacent captures from one walk. The discriminating evidence: a measure, a marker or a caption identifying a fault, or membership in an accepted defect list, supports the snagging row; a record of the state of the works supports this row.

Both are dated photographic condition records. The discriminating evidence: a room-by-room schedule with a signed report and a tenancy or handover purpose supports the inventory row; an open-ended series recording works in progress supports this row. Reciprocal to the edge authored there.

A photographed delivery note and a photograph of a pallet are both site captures. The discriminating evidence: a photographed DOCUMENT, or membership in a delivery group, supports the delivery row; an image of the works supports this row. Reciprocal to the edge authored there.

Photographs are often diary attachments, and a diary entry may contain little beyond them. A dated narrative or structured daily record of labour, weather, plant and events supports site-diary; a deliberately repeated, annotated or issued photographic sequence supports this row. The same embedded or attached images may evidence both. A diary date, site name or work stage is a value shared by both and discriminates neither; membership in an accepted diary group supports the relationship without copying those values onto sparse images.

Damage close-ups of machines sit inside progress sets. The discriminating evidence: an accepted group with a hire or a claim supports the plant row; site record photography supports this row. Reciprocal to the edge authored there.

Aerial overflights of a site are progress records taken from a drone, and their EXIF says drone rather than phone. The discriminating evidence: the aircraft's own metadata and flight-log structure supports the drone row; the construction purpose supports this row - which means a site overflight is genuinely both, and neither row should absorb the other.

A photograph of paperwork taken on site is a document capture wearing image metadata. The discriminating evidence: a page-shaped, text-bearing frame supports the scanned-documents row; a scene supports this row.

falls_through_to.why: The primary residual for this row and the right one: an image with no accepted site or event group is exactly what 00 describes. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

The cautious outcome for a capture whose purpose is unresolved - the defect-or-progress close-up, the stripped-EXIF set from a subcontractor, the video walkthrough. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The home for a generated photo report with no accepted group - a document with a durable purpose. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The safe outcome for an unreadable or damaged image archive, and for raw formats the image stack cannot open. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

Named only to route what this row must NOT take: a screenshot of a plan or a message about the site is not site photography. “Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.”

sensitivity_why: Site photography is incidental surveillance. It contains workers' faces and vehicle registrations, neighbouring private property and its occupants, the interiors of private homes when the job is domestic, and GPS accurate to the metre on every frame. It is also, by design, evidence: a set taken before a cover-up exists to be produced in an argument, and photographs of another party's defective work are allegations about identifiable people. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and GPS metadata is on that list by name. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Whether this row should exist at all, or whether progress photography is only an image SOURCE_TYPE carrying a work_type value inside construction_property.construction-project or evidence attached to construction_property.site-diary. This pass rejects the old answer that a different evidence class is sufficient: capture metadata proves capture provenance, not the progress-photo situation. The row is kept more narrowly because a deliberately repeated, annotated or issued photographic record has recognition and privacy behavior that the project and diary defaults do not express, but it must require purpose-bearing structure or an accepted project/diary relationship. The unresolved product choice is whether that difference warrants an independently browsable template or only a detector/grouping profile inside the project or diary, and whether accepted photographs live under the project, under diary dates, or beside both. Date, site and work stage cannot decide because they are values, and no answer may create construction-flavoured copies of photos fields. Joseph's.
